review_reference: Decision relayed by the user in chat on 2026-11-11, answering which rule Outreach campaign management should follow (ADR-045's open question): "Campaign admins only (Recommended)", option B. Any staff member allowed to write campaigns may create one and becomes its admin; only that campaign's own admins open or close it and add members, enforced in outreach-api and in the database. Numbered 0122, the next free number when written (open PRs hold 0109-0111 and 0113-0121); it takes the next free number when it merges. reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs this declaration.
evidence: Single migration 0122_outreach_campaign_admins.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES: (1) CREATE OR REPLACE of outreach.validate_campaign_write() (0077's body, md5 1ac1e424e645378ab6e88a45542fccf9, kept whole) adding, on UPDATE, that the session's membership is an admin member of the campaign, else 42501 'Outreach campaign admin is required'; owner, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path unchanged; a row lock fires no trigger, so 0045's FOR SHARE on registration is unaffected. (2) Two RESTRICTIVE policies on outreach.campaign_members: insert only by an admin member of the campaign, or by its creator seeding themself as the first admin of a campaign with no member; delete only by an admin member. 0038's permissive policies stay. (3) outreach.campaign_staff(uuid) RETURNS TABLE(membership_id uuid, display_name text, campaign_role text), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, platform, auth, identity, outreach, owned by outreach.campaigns' owner, EXECUTE for hid_outreach_runtime only: to a member of the campaign holding outreach.campaign.read at the session facility, its members (identity.staff.full_name and campaign role); to its admins also every active staff membership at the facility (campaign role null); anyone else no row; at most 1000 rows. No table, column, constraint, index, role or other function changes; no row read or written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api refuses outreach.campaign.write, so no API path reaches a campaign write; campaign reads and registrations are unchanged. RELEASE ORDER: apply 0122 before identity-api ships with outreach.campaign.write accepted. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0108 applied (0108's cover md5 6928763d3b69f0e4b4acf96a6a255736); not applied yet; the trigger function's body and attributes as 0077 left them and its trigger present; FORCE RLS on both campaign tables with 0038's policies; identity.staff and staff_facility_memberships not FORCE RLS; the applier may SET ROLE to the owner, which owns the trigger function and has CREATE on schema outreach. POST-CHECKS: the trigger function's attributes and owner, the two restrictive policies, campaign_staff's attributes, result and ACL. PROVED on local PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (created and deleted): every SQL suite on a fresh install of 0001-0108 and 0122; the upgrade rehearsal services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs (HID_REHEARSAL_ADMIN_URL, a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator, baseline 0001-0108, declared exactly 0122); and the new suite and outreach-session-guards on a database whose migrator is NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/outreach-campaign-admins.integration.sql, 24 cases as hid_outreach_api_runtime: an admin opens and closes, an enumerator, a non-member, an admin of another campaign and the creator who is no longer an admin are refused, another clinic changes nothing; a member's FOR SHARE lock still succeeds; an admin adds members and a second admin, an enumerator and a non-member cannot (themselves included), the creator cannot seed into a campaign with members, a creator seeds themself and nobody else; an enumerator removes no member and an admin can; campaign_staff to an admin, a member, a non-member, another clinic and an unknown campaign; the EHR runtime cannot call it. outreach-session-guards.integration.sql: its fixture campaign's creator is seeded as its admin (as createCampaign does) and campaign updates by another membership, or none, now expect the admin refusal; where the trigger's owner does not bypass RLS, A's sessions without direct care are refused as not an admin as well, since the check reads the members under their policies (121 cases in both shapes).
